{"id": "ca50899a-fec1-4f6a-b2f6-3d70713cfe72", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good — a couple of things worth flagging before the full list. The Q Business SDK docs define `AccessDeniedException` for `ChatSync` loosely as *"you don't have access... make sure you have the required permission policies **and user accounts**"* — that phrasing matters, because it tells you this exception can come from two different authorization layers, and `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` only ever covers one of them cleanly.

**Layer 1 — IAM evaluation gaps the simulator doesn't fully replicate**

1. **Service Control Policies / Resource Control Policies** — the IAM simulator only recently (July 2026 console update) started letting you include SCPs in a simulation, and that's opt-in in the console flow. If you ran the classic `simulate-principal-policy` API/CLI call, it evaluates the identity policy + permission boundary (if attached to a real principal) but does **not** automatically pull in org-level SCPs or the newer **Resource Control Policies (RCPs)** unless you explicitly fed them in. An SCP/RCP deny on `qbusiness:*` at the OU/account level is invisible to your test but very real at runtime.
2. **Session policies** — if the caller got here via `sts:AssumeRole` with an inline session policy (common for federated/SSO sessions), that policy narrows the effective permissions at call time but isn't part of what `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` evaluates unless you pass it as an extra policy input. Effective access = identity policy ∩ permission boundary ∩ session policy.
